textRuns.value: Intake pressure describes the operational strain created when a large share of inpatient admissions arrive unplanned, primarily through Emergency and urgent pathways. Unlike scheduled admissions, unplanned intake is unpredictable, time-compressed, and difficult to smooth, forcing facilities to absorb demand immediately.

When unplanned admissions coincide with material encounter volume, they place sustained pressure on ED capacity, bed availability, staffing, and patient flow. As a result, variation in LOS, cost, and downstream performance is less likely to reflect random demand and more likely to reflect how effectively a facility manages intake, flow, and discharge under persistent, unplanned demand.
